conclusion: Felipe's statement is partially correct: distinct User Access Tokens belonging to distinct advertiser users isolate the Graph API user-level call count, but Marketing API throttling is not only per token. It also applies at ad-account, application, Business Use Case, access-tier, mutation-burst, Insights-app and object-edit levels.

recommended_architecture.advertiser_profiles: one distinct advertiser profile per manager
recommended_architecture.user_access_tokens: one token issued for each manager profile
recommended_architecture.storage: one separate 1Password item per manager token
recommended_architecture.registry: bind each account alias to manager, advertiser profile and 1Password item reference; never store the secret value
recommended_architecture.benefit: credential isolation and isolation of Graph API user-level call counts when tokens belong to different users
recommended_architecture.non_bypass: never rotate or multiply tokens to circumvent an ad-account, app, BUC, tier, burst or object-level limit

official_findings.finding: Requests made with a User Access Token count against that user's rolling one-hour call count, and the same user's count can be spread across multiple apps.
Marketing API rate limiting applies to the ad account across the same Business Use Case and depends on the app's Marketing API Access Tier.

Current Marketing API documentation states rate limiting is at ad-account level; mutation burst limiting is per app plus ad-account combination, and concurrent edits are also limited per object and app.
Limited/development access has less quota than Full access; the access tier appears in rate-limit headers and should be read back during onboarding.
Standard Access permissions are limited to app-role users; Advanced Access permissions can be requested from any app user. Development mode can access only users with an app role.
Facebook Login for Business supports User Access Tokens and is the preferred authorization solution for integrations with Meta business tools.

Meta Developer Accounts are required for Administrator, Developer or Analytics roles, while Tester invitations can be sent to regular users; Authorized App Testers can accept an invitation and grant permissions during development.
